clue.text: Two pieces performed by minor player

definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer, a role a minor player performs

blocks.note: a bit is a piece, the first of the two
a part is a piece, the second of the two

explanation.surface: A musician plays a couple of short numbers as a junior member of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two pieces' supplies both halves, BIT and PART; the rest of the clue describes the answer rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit part is a small acting role, the kind of thing a minor player in a cast performs.

clue.text: Boy threw up having applied small drop

blocks.note: B is an abbreviation for boy
to lob is to throw high into the air

explanation.surface: A lad was sick after taking a small dose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Threw up' suggests vomiting but means tossed upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A blob is a small drop of liquid, so to have blobbed is to have dabbed a drop on.

clue.text: Rush job on cottage?

setter's reading: work using rushes or reeds to cover a cottage roof

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush job' reads as hasty work; rushes are reeds, used to roof cottages.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatching is covering a roof with straw or reeds such as rushes, typical of country cottages.

clue.text: Pal's fibs built central part of criminal defence

indicators.note: central asks for the middle of each word, its core letters

blocks.note: the middle two of four
the middle two of four
the middle letter of five

explanation.surface: A friend's lies formed the core of a criminal's defence case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Built' is both a word to mine and the joining verb in the surface; its centre is the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere when a crime occurred, a key element of a defence.

clue.text: Stoical view when the flat is turned over

explanation.definitionFit: That's life is the shrugging remark of someone accepting misfortune calmly, a stoic attitude.

clue.text: Shot into the air when excited

blocks.note: first meaning: discharged upwards, as a gun or rocket
second meaning: enthused, stirred into action

explanation.surface: Someone loses control and fires a gun skyward in a moment of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal sense of firing a weapon upwards and the idiomatic sense of being enthused share one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fired up is an idiom for being eager and enthusiastic, while a rocket fired up has been launched skyward.

clue.text: Nothing capital university put together is wrong

blocks.note: sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all
the London School of Economics, a university in the capital

explanation.surface: Claiming the London university built nothing is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is British slang meaning nothing; the LSE is a London university.
explanation.definitionFit: False means untrue or incorrect, so it is a synonym of wrong.

clue.text: Surprise stronghold, reportedly something crumbly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, not as it is written

blocks.note: to rock is to shock or surprise

explanation.surface: A surprise attack on a fortress is said to have left it crumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: this crumbly thing is a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Roquefort is a French blue cheese made from ewe's milk, with a soft crumbly texture.

clue.text: Fourth rate swinger perhaps out for a duck

blocks.note: the fourth grade, after A, B and C
a rake is a womaniser, a swinging type

explanation.surface: A poor cricket batter, swinging wildly, is out without scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out for a duck' is cricket for dismissed without scoring, but here the duck is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, so an example of the bird.

clue.text: Hunt for food before meeting with romantic partner

blocks.note: pre means before
a date is a romantic meeting

explanation.surface: Someone forages for a meal ahead of an evening out with their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay also means come earlier, a second sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To predate is to act as a predator, catching other animals to eat.

clue.text: Fine detective captures a forest creature

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside, so one piece is held within the others

blocks.note: OK means fine, all right
PI is a private investigator
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good detective manages to catch a woodland animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The container is the pair 'Fine detective' read together: the A sits between the two pieces rather than inside the detective alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a giraffe relative living in the rainforests of central Africa, so an example of a forest creature.

clue.text: Drawing a description of chessboard

blocks.note: first meaning: level in a contest, neither side ahead
second meaning: a board made entirely of squares

explanation.surface: A sketch is made portraying a chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' looks like a picture, but here it is the present participle of draw, being level in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: All square is the idiom for a tied score, and literally a chessboard is nothing but squares.

clue.text: Old magazine spreading sick abuse

indicators.note: something spreading is scattered about, so the letters are dispersed and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An old tabloid publication is passing around nasty abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A back issue is an earlier edition of a periodical, no longer the current one.

clue.text: Part of mainframe needs backing up – it will remove waste

indicators.note: a part of the following words is taken, a run of letters sitting inside them
in a down-style reading, backing up means going backwards, so the run is read in reverse

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A computer's central unit needs backing up, as the backup will clear out junk files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing up' sounds like computer data protection; it is the instruction to read the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is a procedure that flushes out the bowel, so it removes bodily waste.

clue.text: Doctor I have contracted to provide spin

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
the contraction I've, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A doctor says they have signed a contract to give a public-relations spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' suggests signing up for work; it means shortened, as I have becomes I've.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is an informal word for a short trip in a car, which is a drive.

clue.text: Old style master abandons median location for medical facility

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so that letter is dropped
the word before is the place where the next piece is put, its middle

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for master
taken as written
a hospital ward

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned master leaves the central site for a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Losing M leaves EDIAN, and WARD goes into its median position, giving EDWARDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwardian describes the style of the reign of Edward VII, from 1901 to 1910, so old-fashioned.

clue.text: Cooking native oil is perfectly safe

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into something new

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Frying with local oil is claimed to be completely harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inviolate means untouched and unbroken, never harmed or violated, hence wholly secure.

clue.text: Doctor may covet adopting son; it avoids having another?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
S is the abbreviation for son, added to the mix

explanation.surface: A doctor might wish to adopt a son, avoiding the need to have another baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adopting' brings the son into the letters before they are rearranged; the question mark marks the cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vasectomy is male sterilisation, preventing a man from fathering any more children.

clue.text: Writer checks out reports of sanction

indicators.note: reports are what is heard, so the next words are taken by sound

blocks.note: an author is a writer
to eye someone is to check them out

explanation.surface: An author reviews accounts of official penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanction' can mean a penalty, but here it is the verb to permit.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise is to give official permission, which is what sanction means as a verb.

clue.text: They may have boxers leave when getting into drugs?

indicators.note: one thing getting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: downers are sedative drugs
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Boxers quit the ring when they get mixed up with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' suggests fighters, but they are the dog breed; the question mark flags that boxers are just one example of what these people keep.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers are a breed of dog, so people who own dogs may have boxers as pets.

clue.text: Came together when I left after father gets intimidated

indicators.note: left here means departed, so that letter goes

blocks.note: da is an informal word for dad
united means joined up
taken as written, removed

explanation.surface: People united, but one was left cowed after a parent stepped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Daunted means discouraged or made fearful, so a synonym of intimidated.

clue.text: Bags, totally shorter for the younger generation

definitions.text: totally shorter for the younger generation

blocks.note: first meaning: tote bags, carriers

blocks.clueFragment: totally shorter for the younger generation
blocks.note: second meaning: youth slang clipping the adverb meaning completely

explanation.surface: Young people say bags are totally in, using shorter words.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half describes the word: young people clip 'totally' to a slang form meaning absolutely.
explanation.definitionFit: Totes are large carrier bags, and totes is also teenage slang for definitely or completely.

clue.text: Academic check into potentially free form of energy

indicators.note: into puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: sunshine costs nothing, so solar power is potentially free
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A professor investigates renewable power.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person engaged in study, a noun sense of academic.

clue.text: Losing against opposition that's game?

blocks.note: a losing side is down; its opposite is up
the opposite of against is for

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the match was the one lost to the other team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposition' tells you to take the opposite of each word: losing means down, so UP; against becomes FOR. It reads like a sports report.
explanation.definitionFit: To be game is to be willing to try something, and up for is the informal idiom for the same eagerness.

clue.text: Spicy and extremely intense ingredient of greasy food

blocks.note: a fry is a fried meal
the first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: Fiery describes food that is strongly spiced, giving a burning sensation, so hot or spicy.

clue.text: Fire idiot with heroin – it's rough stuff

clot is British slang for a fool
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Sack the fool caught with heroin, as that is bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough stuff' sounds like violence, but it describes a coarse fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Sackcloth is a coarse woven fabric, traditionally worn in penance, so literally rough material.

clue.text: Attack credit record

blocks.note: first meaning: criticise harshly
second meaning: a tab
third meaning: a list of past performance

clue.text: Twist what he is really like at first

clue.text: Phrase regularly re-used in time when spouse requires affirmation?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a year is a period of time
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A long-married person keeps repeating the same words whenever their partner wants agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a whole-clue description, yet 'Phrase' is only a pointer that the answer is a saying, and the definition is the closing situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes dear is the stock henpecked reply, agreeing with whatever the other half says without real engagement.
